title: AXI4-Lite Interface Surface
description: Inspect the five retained channels and the controls AXI4-Lite fixes or removes; each entry highlights the direction, transfer edge, and a common subset-verification trap.

signals.name: AW channel
signals.description: The write-address channel retains the normal handshake, byte address, and protection attributes. AWPROT is part of the permitted AXI4-Lite signal set.
signals.direction: AWVALID/AWADDR/AWPROT: master to slave; AWREADY: slave to master
signals.sampled: Rising ACLK edge with AWVALID and AWREADY HIGH
signals.verificationNote: Do not drop protection checking merely because AWCACHE is absent; AXI4-Lite conversion passes AxPROT through.

signals.name: W channel
signals.description: Each write transaction carries one full-bus-width transfer. WSTRB still qualifies byte lanes and can support sparse register updates according to the slave's documented behavior.
signals.direction: WVALID/WDATA/WSTRB: master to slave; WREADY: slave to master
signals.sampled: Rising ACLK edge with WVALID and WREADY HIGH
signals.verificationNote: AW and W remain independent channels; a Lite slave must not assume their handshakes occur together.

signals.name: B channel
signals.description: The slave returns one write response after the accepted address and data. OKAY, SLVERR, and DECERR remain meaningful; EXOKAY is not supported.
signals.direction: BVALID/BRESP: slave to master; BREADY: master to slave
signals.sampled: Rising ACLK edge with BVALID and BREADY HIGH
signals.verificationNote: Multiple requests can be outstanding even without protocol IDs; responses must remain in order.

signals.name: AR channel
signals.description: The read-address channel mirrors the Lite write-address subset and retains ARPROT while omitting burst, size, lock, and cache controls.
signals.direction: ARVALID/ARADDR/ARPROT: master to slave; ARREADY: slave to master
signals.sampled: Rising ACLK edge with ARVALID and ARREADY HIGH
signals.verificationNote: Check AR independently from R; a design can accept more than one address before returning data if it preserves order.

signals.name: R channel
signals.description: Each read response is one full-bus-width transfer. RLAST is implied for the single transfer and therefore omitted from the interface.
signals.direction: RVALID/RDATA/RRESP: slave to master; RREADY: master to slave
signals.sampled: Rising ACLK edge with RVALID and RREADY HIGH
signals.verificationNote: Hold RVALID, RDATA, and RRESP stable during read-data backpressure just as on full AXI4.

signals.name: Fixed subset
signals.expansion: Burst length 1 and full bus width
signals.description: AXI4-Lite omits AxLEN, AxSIZE, and AxBURST because every transaction has one transfer defined to use the 32- or 64-bit interface width.
signals.sampled: The subset behavior applies to every accepted transaction
signals.verificationNote: WSTRB can still select bytes; do not mistake sparse strobes for a narrower AxSIZE transfer on the Lite interface.

signals.name: IDs and ordering
signals.description: AXI4-Lite does not use AXI IDs for reordering, so transactions complete in order. Optional ID reflection can exist for direct interoperability with a full AXI connection.
signals.direction: Normally no ID signals on a pure AXI4-Lite interface
signals.sampled: Allocate and retire requests in issue order
signals.verificationNote: No IDs does not mean only one outstanding transaction; use handshakes to enforce any smaller implementation limit.

signals.name: LOCK and CACHE
signals.description: AXI4-Lite omits AxLOCK and AxCACHE. Accesses are Normal rather than exclusive, and are defined as Non-modifiable and Non-bufferable.
signals.sampled: Fixed attributes apply to every transaction
signals.verificationNote: Keep this distinction separate from AxPROT, which remains available for privilege, security, and instruction/data attributes.
